title: Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999
text: The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999, provides for the registration and better protection of geographical indications relating to goods in India. A Geographical Indication (GI) identifies agricultural, natural, or manufactured goods as originating in a specific territory where a given quality, reputation, or other characteristic of the goods is essentially attributable to its geographical origin. For example, Jaipur Blue Pottery and Madhubani Painting hold active GI tags.

title: Jaipur Blue Pottery History & Materials
text: Jaipur Blue Pottery is unique because it is made without clay. Instead, it uses a paste made of ground quartz stone, glass powder, fuller's earth (Multani Mitti), borax, gum, and water. The glaze is also lead-free and traditionally colored using cobalt oxide for blue and copper oxide for green. The craft was introduced to Jaipur by Maharaja Sawai Ram Singh II in the 19th century and has a registered GI status.

title: Madhubani Painting Traditional Heritage
text: Madhubani painting (or Mithila painting) is practiced in the Mithila region of Bihar, India. Painting is traditionally done by women using natural pigments and dyes extracted from plants, flowers, charcoal, and ochre. The paintings feature complex geometrical patterns and portray scenes from ancient epics, nature, and social celebrations. It has received a GI tag to prevent duplicate machine prints from counterfeiting traditional hand-crafted paintings.

title: Kashmir Pashmina Standards
text: Authentic Kashmir Pashmina wool is sourced from the undercoat of the Changthangi goat (Capra hircus) native to the high-altitude Ladakh region. The fibers must be hand-spun and hand-woven on traditional wooden looms in Kashmir. The fiber diameter must be under 15 microns. Genuine Pashmina items receive GI certification, ensuring protection against machine-made viscose or polyester counterfeits sold as wool.

title: Government Support Policies for Artisans
text: The Ministry of Textiles in India offers several financial, marketing, and developmental support schemes for artisans. The Ambedkar Hastshilp Vikas Yojana (AHVY) aims to empower artisans by organizing them into self-help groups and guilds. The National Handicrafts Development Programme (NHDP) supports marketing platforms, exhibitions, and provides direct bank credits. Mudra loans are also accessible under the MSME category to finance artisan workshops.

title: Registered GI Handicrafts of India (Registry Summary)
text: India's GI registry records 255 handicraft geographical indications (JusticeHub extract, registrations 2004-2005 to 2023-2024). States with the most registered handicraft GIs include Uttar Pradesh (34), Tamil Nadu (33), Karnataka (20), Gujarat (16), Kerala (15). Each registered craft links its origin state to a GI certification tag, which is how Viraasat verifies artisan provenance.
